incident_findings: R3 observed five task positions reach the 8192-token cap, so the R3 Pilot did not cover the formal tail of response complexity.
R3 auto-resume reran infrastructure-invalid task positions and reapplied the per-process retry budget.
The final tau3 raw result omitted user-simulator calls belonging to discarded or interrupted attempts.
The local proxy endpoint 127.0.0.1:10823 was unavailable during the first invocation while a direct unauthenticated provider health request remained reachable.
acceptance_basis: 32768 is four times the observed R3 cap and remains one eighth of the pinned provider adapter's documented default output limit.
The output-budget change is symmetric for baseline and every later candidate and does not change Objective, Split, Gate, tasks, trials, model, temperature, or evaluator.
The global attempt cap preserves the registered initial-plus-one-retry topology across process interruption and resume.
Separate append-only agent and user ledgers preserve known model costs outside retained final simulations.
Valid-run exact cost remains a hard Gate; whole-attempt partial accounting is reported as a lower bound with unknown scopes and is never treated as zero or used for candidate ranking.
limitations: The 32768-token control is incident-driven and has not yet been validated by a paid R4 formal run.
A provider failure without terminal usage may still leave an unknown billing scope even though the started call remains recorded.
Local compute monetary cost remains unmetered; wall, user CPU, system CPU, and maximum resident set must be recorded separately.
Direct routing is frozen only for the R4 subprocess environment and does not assert that all developer networks should bypass proxies.
